canonical_topic: Seasonality of the natural gas forward curve
definition: Natural gas forward prices are driven by seasonal expectations of supply and demand rather than by the current spot price and storage costs, producing a forward curve that is highly cyclical (high in winter, falling sharply in spring) rather than smoothly upward-sloping.
core_idea: Because seasonal supply-demand patterns repeat similarly year to year, the gas forward curve tracks the seasonal shape of consumer demand instead of following the interest-rate/storage-cost-driven slope typical of other storable-commodity forward curves.
key_points: Seasonal supply-demand expectations tend to repeat similarly from year to year.
Forward prices mirror consumer demand seasonality — high in winter, falling dramatically in spring.
This cyclical shape contrasts with markets where forward prices are set by interest rates and storage costs, which tend to produce a different relationship (referenced in the source as Figure 2.1.8).
relationships: Connects to time spreads (which trade this seasonal shape) and to the storable-commodity contrast
trading_implications: Time-spread traders can structure positions around the expected, recurring seasonal shape of the curve.
